history.title: Run until time budget, not 10 steps
history.patch:
# Run until time budget, not 10 steps
Hypothesis: all four transcripts end "returned" after exactly 10 model calls and only 18-32 s of the 180 s budget; the model was still exploring (listing files, checking tools) when the step cap cut it off.
Change: MAX_STEPS 10 -> 100 as a safety net; the loop now stops when env.time_left() drops below a 10 s margin.
Expected: tasks needing more than 10 commands (build, recovery, multi-step data work) get time to finish; could burn time on hopeless tasks, or hit the time limit mid-command.

history.title: Show stderr and the tail of outputs
history.patch:
# Show stderr and the tail of outputs
Hypothesis: failures (build-pov-ray, financial-document-processor) lost information: stderr was discarded and long outputs were cut to the first 1000 chars, so compiler/linker errors (printed last) and tool diagnostics were hidden and the model guessed or looped.
Change: commands run with 2>&1; output limit 1000 -> 3000 chars, and over-long output keeps head and tail with a "chars cut" marker.
Expected: fewer blind retries on build/tool errors, faster fixes; could cost more input tokens per step and add some stderr noise.

history.title: Show the clock, force delivery near deadline
history.patch:
# Show the clock, force delivery near deadline
Hypothesis: the model never sees the time budget; in financial-document-processor it spent 172 s of 180 s on OCR of one unreadable file and produced no output at all (also build-pov-ray finished unverified), so partial credit was impossible.
Change: every tool result gets a "[time left: N s]" line; under 70 s left it adds a WRAP UP NOW instruction to write all required outputs with best guesses and finish.
Expected: fixes tasks that die mid-investigation with nothing delivered (financial-document-processor-style rabbit holes); could make the model quit too early on hard builds or write low-quality guesses.

history.title: Show stderr only when a command fails
history.patch:
# Show stderr only when a command fails
Hypothesis: stderr is thrown away, so failing commands return exit 2 and empty or vague output (build-pov-ray: compiler/linker errors hidden, repeated blind retries; financial-document-processor: tool failures invisible during OCR attempts).
Change: stderr goes to a side file; when the exit code is non-zero the last 1500 chars of it are appended to the tool result. Successful commands look exactly as before.
Expected: fixes blind retries after failed builds and tool calls; unlike iteration 2 it adds no stderr noise or output-size change on successful commands, but failing commands cost a few more tokens.

history.title: Verify requirements before declaring done
history.patch:
# Verify requirements before declaring done
Hypothesis: build-pov-ray ended with a confident "build complete" summary after only a sanity run and still got reward 0; the model never re-checked the task's explicit requirements (paths, names, formats) before stopping.
Change: the first time the model answers without a tool call (and 40+ s remain), the harness adds one user message asking it to list each explicit requirement and verify each by command; the second text answer ends the run.
Expected: fixes premature "done" claims with a missed requirement (build-pov-ray-style); could cost 10-20 s on tasks already correct, and does not help rabbit holes like financial-document-processor.

history.title: Deliver early, switch approach, never stall
history.patch:
# Deliver early, switch approach, never stall
Hypothesis: financial-document-processor spent ~25 of 53 calls retrying OCR variants on one unreadable file and delivered nothing; build-pov-ray also ended unchecked against the task's wording. The model has no working discipline in its prompt.
Change: SYSTEM_PROMPT gains four working rules: deliver a rough complete result first, switch approach after two failures or ~5 commands on one item, best guess beats missing output, check the exact task wording at the end.
Expected: fixes rabbit holes that end with nothing delivered (partial credit, skipped hard items); could make the model give up on a hard step too early or add a few seconds of final checking.

history.title: Periodic progress checkpoint in tool results
history.patch:
# Periodic progress checkpoint in tool results
Hypothesis: financial-document-processor spent ~45 calls on OCR variants of one file and delivered nothing; build-pov-ray declared done without tracking what remained. Static prompt rules (iter 6) and a late deadline warning (iter 3) did not work; the model needs a recurring in-context prompt to take stock.
Change: every 8th tool call, the tool result gets a checkpoint note with command count and time left, asking the model to state what is done/remaining and to drop a stuck sub-problem with a best guess.
Expected: fixes rabbit holes that end with nothing delivered (partial output earlier); could hurt hard tasks needing long single-problem persistence, and adds a few tokens per 8 steps.

+    "which parts of the task are DONE and written to the required place, and which remain. "

@@ -58,4 +67,7 @@

+            calls += 1

history.title: Detect repeated-command loops, force new approach
history.patch:
# Detect repeated-command loops, force new approach
Hypothesis: financial-document-processor spent 25+ calls re-running tesseract variants on one unreadable file and delivered nothing; build-pov-ray also repeated near-identical fix attempts.
Change: the harness records the main program of each command; after 4 consecutive commands with the same program, the tool result gets a note telling the model to switch tool/method or accept the best result and finish other outputs.
Expected: cuts OCR/tuning rabbit holes so other outputs get delivered; could misfire on legitimate repeated use (many `sed`/`cat` edits) and nudge the model off a fine path.

 """
 
 import json
+import re
 
 SYSTEM_PROMPT = """You are an AI agent that solves tasks in a Linux terminal.
 Use the bash tool to run commands. When the task is complete, reply with a short summary."""
@@ -43,7 +44,23 @@

+def main_program(command):
+    """The program name of the last command in a pipeline or && chain."""
+    last = re.split(r"&&|\|\||[|;]", command.strip())[-1].split()
+    return last[0] if last else ""
+
+
+def stuck_note(history):
+    """After 4 commands in a row with the same main program, tell the model to change approach."""
+    if len(history) >= 4 and len(set(history[-4:])) == 1:
+        return (f"\n[harness: your last 4 commands all ran `{history[-1]}` and results are not improving. "
+                "Try a different tool or method, or accept the best result so far "
+                "and finish the other required outputs.]")
+    return ""
+
+
 def run(task, env):
+    history = []
     messages = [
         {"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM_PROMPT},
         {"role": "user", "content": task},
@@ -58,4 +75,6 @@
             return  # the model answered in text: we are done
         for call in tool_calls:
             content = run_tool_call(call, env)
+            history.append(main_program(json.loads(call["function"]["arguments"])["command"]))
+            content += stuck_note(history)
             messages.append({"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": call["id"], "content": content})
